note: The narrator's lines, one entry per shot of the shot table in matchlight_scene.h, in order. Written for this film in its own words from the story beats of Hans Christian Andersen's public-domain tale (1845); no translation is quoted. tools/narration.py turns them into the on-screen subtitles and, with a recording, into the voice track.

lines.text: It is New Year's Eve, and the cold is deep. Snow falls on the dark street. Other people's windows glow. Nobody stops.
A girl walks in from the far end. She has sold no matches all day. She does not dare go home.
She lost her slippers in the road, when two carriages rushed past.
She strikes a match. Its light is warm: an iron stove, with a fire blazing. Then the light goes out.
The match goes out. The cold comes back.
She stays out in the cold, and sits down in the snow. Nobody comes.
She strikes a second match. A roast goose steams on its dish.
A third match. A Christmas tree, with candles on every branch. The candles rise, and they look like stars.
A star falls: a soul going to heaven.
A fourth match. Her grandmother appears, the only one who ever loved her.
Now she strikes the whole bundle at once. It is brighter than day. Her grandmother takes her hand. No cold, no hunger.
On New Year's morning, people find her, almost smiling. They do not know what she saw. Snow covers her.
